title: Les‿amis
en: Pronunciation: liaison and linking words together
intro: In French, the words of a group flow together with no gaps. A final consonant that is normally **silent** is sometimes pronounced when the next word starts with a vowel: **les amis** = /le.za.mi/. This is **liaison**. Some liaisons are compulsory, some are forbidden, and getting them right makes you sound French straight away.

cases.label: when you must link
cases.rule: Always link a **determiner + noun** (*les‿amis, un‿ami*), a **pronoun + verb** (*nous‿avons, ils‿aiment*), an **adjective + noun** (*petit‿enfant*), after short words like *très, chez, dans, en*, and in set phrases (*tout‿à coup*).

cases.label: s, x, z → /z/
cases.rule: A final **s, x** or **z** links as /z/: *les‿amis* /le.za.mi/, *deux‿enfants* /dø.zɑ̃.fɑ̃/, *chez‿eux* /ʃe.zø/.

cases.label: t, d → /t/
cases.rule: A final **t** or **d** links as /t/: *c'est‿un* /sɛ.tœ̃/, *quand‿il* /kɑ̃.til/, *un grand‿homme* /ɡʁɑ̃.tɔm/.

cases.label: n → /n/
cases.rule: A final **n** links as /n/: *un‿ami* /œ̃.na.mi/, *mon‿ami, on‿a, en‿été*.

cases.label: f → /v/, r → /ʁ/
cases.rule: Two rarer ones: **neuf** links with /v/ in *neuf‿ans* and *neuf‿heures*, and **premier, dernier** link with /ʁ/: *le premier‿étage*.

cases.label: when you must NOT link
cases.rule: Never link after **et** (*un café et | un thé*), after a **singular noun** (*un étudiant | anglais*), or before an **h aspiré** (*les | héros*) or **onze** (*les | onze joueurs*).

cases.label: ils‿ont or ils sont?
cases.rule: Liaison can change the meaning: *ils‿ont* /il.zɔ̃/ (they have) but *ils sont* /il.sɔ̃/ (they are). Listen for /z/ or /s/!

cases.label: enchaînement
cases.rule: A final consonant that you **always** say slides onto the next vowel: *il‿est* /i.lɛ/, *elle‿a* /ɛ.la/, *une‿amie* /y.na.mi/, *avec‿elle*. No new sound appears: the words just run together.

sections.title: 1. Liaison: when you must link
text: Most final consonants in French are silent: *les* /le/, *petit* /pə.ti/, *deux* /dø/. But when the next word starts with a **vowel** or a **silent h**, the consonant is pronounced at the start of the next word. Inside these word groups, liaison is compulsory:

examples.en: The children are playing in the park.

sections.tip: Compare: *les parents* /le.pa.ʁɑ̃/ (a consonant: no liaison) and *les‿amis* /le.za.mi/.

sections.title: 2. s, x, z → /z/
text: The most common liaison. Whether it's written **s**, **x** or **z**, it always sounds **/z/**.
sections.tip: The **x** of *deux, six, dix* also sounds /z/: *six‿ans* /si.zɑ̃/, *dix‿euros* /di.zø.ʁo/.

sections.title: 3. t, d → /t/

examples.fr: {Quand il|lia-t} pleut, je reste à la maison.
examples.en: When it rains, I stay at home.

sections.tip: A final **d** becomes /t/: *grand‿homme* /ɡʁɑ̃.tɔm/, *quand‿il* /kɑ̃.til/. And careful: *un petit‿ami* means *a boyfriend*!

sections.title: 4. n → /n/
text: After **un, mon, ton, son, on, en, rien**, the **n** is heard before a vowel. The vowel before it usually stays nasal: *un‿ami* /œ̃.na.mi/.

sections.title: 5. Two rare ones: /v/ and /ʁ/
text: **neuf** links with a **/v/** in *neuf ans* and *neuf heures*. And **premier, dernier** link with an **/ʁ/**.

examples.en: The class starts at nine o'clock.
I live on the first floor.

sections.title: 6. When you must NOT link
text: Some liaisons are forbidden, and making them is a typical learner's mistake.

examples.fr: Un croissant {et un|lia-never} café, s'il vous plaît.
examples.en: A croissant and a coffee, please.

examples.fr: {Les héros|lia-never} du film sont des enfants.
examples.en: The heroes of the film are children.

sections.tip: An **h aspiré** is silent too, but it blocks liaison and elision: *le héros, la Hollande, le hockey*. Dictionaries mark these words with a symbol, often an asterisk.

sections.title: 7. ils‿ont or ils sont?
text: Here, liaison changes the meaning. Listen to the sound before the vowel: **/z/** in *ils‿ont* (they have), **/s/** in *ils sont* (they are).
sections.tip: The same thing happens with *nous‿avons* /nu.za.vɔ̃/ (we have) and *nous savons* /nu.sa.vɔ̃/ (we know).

sections.title: 8. Enchaînement: words that run together
text: When a word ends with a consonant that you **always** pronounce (*il, elle, avec, une, quatre*), that consonant slides onto the next vowel. Nothing new is added; there's just no gap. This is called **enchaînement**.

examples.en: I'm going to the cinema with her.

sections.tip: French flows from syllable to syllable: *Il est à Paris* sounds like one long word: /i.lɛ.ta.pa.ʁi/.

mistakes.why: Liaison is compulsory after a determiner.
Link a number to its noun.
**h aspiré**: no liaison. (*les zéros* means *the zeros*!)

story.title: Un dîner entre amis
story.en: Léa and Sophie have friends round for dinner. Listen for the links between the words.

lines.fr: Samedi soir, Léa et Sophie font un dîner pour {leurs amis|lia-must}.
lines.en: On Saturday evening, Léa and Sophie are having a dinner for their friends.

lines.fr: À {neuf heures|lia-rare}, on sonne à la porte : ce sont {les invités|lia-z} !
lines.en: At nine o'clock, the doorbell rings: it's the guests!
Good evening, Inès! Good evening, Carla! How are you?

lines.fr: Très bien, merci ! Oh, {vous avez|lia-z} beaucoup de fleurs sur le balcon !
lines.en: Very well, thank you! Oh, you've got lots of flowers on the balcony!

lines.fr: Puis Tom arrive avec {un ami|lia-n}, Oscar. C'est {un étudiant anglais|lia-never}.
lines.en: Then Tom arrives with a friend, Oscar. He's an English student.

lines.fr: Je vous présente Oscar. {Il habite|lia-ench} à Lyon depuis {deux ans|lia-z}.
lines.en: Let me introduce Oscar. He's been living in Lyon for two years.

lines.fr: Bonsoir ! Je suis très content d'être ici.
lines.en: Good evening! I'm very happy to be here.

lines.fr: Hugo arrive en retard, bien sûr, à dix heures… avec {un énorme gâteau|lia-n} !
lines.en: Hugo arrives late, of course, at ten o'clock… with an enormous cake!
Sorry! It's a cake for my friends!

lines.fr: Le dîner est prêt ! Il y a du poulet {et un|lia-never} gratin… avec {des haricots|lia-never} verts.
lines.en: Dinner's ready! There's chicken and a gratin… with green beans.

lines.fr: Mmm, c'est délicieux ! En Angleterre, on ne mange pas comme ça !
lines.en: Mmm, it's delicious! In England, we don't eat like this!

lines.fr: Après le dîner, on regarde le match ? {Les onze|lia-never} joueurs de Lyon sont {mes héros|lia-never} !
lines.en: After dinner, shall we watch the match? The eleven Lyon players are my heroes!

lines.fr: Le foot ? Non, Hugo ! Ce soir, on danse !
lines.en: Football? No, Hugo! Tonight, we're dancing!

lines.fr: {Tout à coup|lia-must}, la musique commence. Tout le monde [danse|danser].
lines.en: Suddenly, the music starts. Everyone dances.

lines.fr: {Ils sont|lia-zs} contents : {ils ont|lia-zs} des amis formidables !
lines.en: They're happy: they have wonderful friends!

quiz.q: A liaison can happen when the next word starts with…
options: a vowel or a silent h
quiz.answer: a vowel or a silent h

quiz.q: In « les amis », do you pronounce the s?
Listen: which sound links the two words?
In « chez eux », the z sounds…
Listen: which sound links « grand » and « homme »?
In « quand il pleut », the d sounds…
Listen: which sound links the two words?
Listen: how does « neuf » link to « heures »?
In « le premier étage », the r of « premier »…
« un café et un thé »: do you link « et » and « un »?

quiz.why: With a liaison, it would sound like *les zéros* (the zeros)!

quiz.q: « un étudiant anglais »: do you link « étudiant » and « anglais »?
options: no: never after a singular noun
quiz.answer: no: never after a singular noun

quiz.q: Listen: ils ont or ils sont?
Listen: elles ont or elles sont?
